46	static void add_delaylist(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem,
47	                          bool asan_check)
48	{
49	#if defined(CONFIG_BUILD_FLAT) || defined(__KERNEL__)
50	  FAR struct mm_delayhead_s *delay = get_delayhead(heap);
51	  FAR struct mm_delaynode_s *tmp = mem;
52	  irqstate_t flags;
53	  bool bypass;
54	
55	  /* Delay the deallocation until a more appropriate time. */
56	
57	  flags = up_irq_save();
58	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
59	
60	#ifdef CONFIG_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS
61	  /* Check for double-free:
62	   * Step 1: Check magic first (fast path, filters 99.99% cases)
63	   * Step 2: If magic matches, verify it's actually in delay list
64	   *         (slow path, handles extreme case where user data == magic)
65	   */
66	
67	  if (tmp->magic == ~(uintptr_t)mem)
68	    {
69	      /* Magic matches, but could be false positive from user data.
70	       * Traverse delay list to confirm this is really a duplicate.
71	       */
72	
73	      FAR struct mm_delaynode_s *node;
74	
75	      for (node = delay->head; node != NULL; node = node->flink)
76	        {
77	          if (node == tmp)
78	            {
79	              /* Confirmed: this memory is already in delay list.
80	               * This is a real double-free!
81	               */
82	
83	              kasan_bypass(bypass);
84	              up_irq_restore(flags);
85	              DEBUGASSERT(false);  /* Double-free detected! */
86	              return;
87	            }
88	        }
89	
90	      /* Magic matched but not in list - just user data coincidence.
91	       * Continue with normal flow.
92	       */
93	    }
94	
95	#  ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
96	  if (!heap->mm_mpool || !mempool_multiple_member(heap->mm_mpool, mem))
97	#  endif
98	    {
99	      FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
100	      node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)mem -
101	             MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
102	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node));
103	    }
104	
105	  tmp->magic = ~(uintptr_t)mem;
106	#endif
107	
108	  tmp->flink  = delay->head;
109	  delay->head = tmp;
110	
111	#if CONFIG_MM_FREE_DELAYCOUNT_MAX > 0
112	  delay->delaycount++;
113	#endif

117	      size_t size = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
118	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
119	      memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, size);
120	#endif
121	      UNUSED(size);
122	      kasan_poison(mem, size);
123	    }

127	#endif

142	void mm_forcefree(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, FAR void *mem)
143	{
144	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *node;
145	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev;
146	  FAR struct mm_freenode_s *next;
147	  size_t nodesize;
148	  size_t prevsize;
149	  bool bypass;
150	
151	  /* Free mempool blk first */
152	
153	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
154	  if (heap->mm_mpool && mempool_multiple_free(heap->mm_mpool, mem) >= 0)
155	    {
156	      return;
157	    }
158	#endif
159	
160	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
161	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
162	  nodesize = mm_malloc_size(heap, mem);
163	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_FILL_ALLOCATIONS
164	  memset(mem, MM_FREE_MAGIC, nodesize);
165	#endif
166	  kasan_poison(mem, nodesize);
167	
168	  /* Map the memory chunk into a free node */
169	
170	  node = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
171	         ((FAR char *)kasan_clear_tag(mem) - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
172	  nodesize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
173	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_RECORD_STACK
174	  backtrace_remove(node->stack);
175	#endif
176	
177	  /* Sanity check against double-frees */
178	
179	  if (MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node))
180	    {
181	      mm_trace_diag(DIAG_MM_FREE_FAIL, "address:%p, reason:%s",
182	                    mem, "double-free");
183	    }
184	
185	  DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_ALLOC(node));
186	  node->size &= ~MM_ALLOC_BIT;
187	
188	  /* Update heap statistics */
189	
190	  heap->mm_curused -= nodesize;
191	  sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_FREE, heap, mem, nodesize, heap->mm_curused);
192	
193	  /* Check if the following node is free and, if so, merge it */
194	
195	  next = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)node + nodesize);
196	  DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_ALLOC(next));
197	  if (MM_NODE_IS_FREE(next))
198	    {
199	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *andbeyond;
200	      size_t nextsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(next);
201	
202	      /* Get the node following the next node (which will
203	       * become the new next node). We know that we can never
204	       * index past the tail chunk because it is always allocated.
205	       */
206	
207	      andbeyond = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)((FAR char *)next + nextsize);
208	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(andbeyond) &&
209	                  andbeyond->preceding == nextsize);
210	
211	      /* Remove the next node.  There must be a predecessor,
212	       * but there may not be a successor node.
213	       */
214	
215	      DEBUGASSERT(next->blink);
216	      next->blink->flink = next->flink;
217	      if (next->flink)
218	        {
219	          next->flink->blink = next->blink;
220	        }
221	
222	      /* Then merge the two chunks */
223	
224	      nodesize            += nextsize;
225	      node->size           = nodesize | (node->size & MM_MASK_BIT);
226	      andbeyond->preceding = nodesize;
227	      next                 = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)andbeyond;
228	    }
229	  else
230	    {
231	      next->size     |= MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
232	      next->preceding = nodesize;
233	    }
234	
235	  /* Check if the preceding node is also free and, if so, merge
236	   * it with this node
237	   */
238	
239	  if (MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node))
240	    {
241	      prev = (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)
242	        ((FAR char *)node - node->preceding);
243	      prevsize = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(prev);
244	      DEBUGASSERT(MM_NODE_IS_FREE(prev) && node->preceding == prevsize);
245	
246	      /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may
247	       * not be a successor node.
248	       */
249	
250	      DEBUGASSERT(prev->blink);
251	      prev->blink->flink = prev->flink;
252	      if (prev->flink)
253	        {
254	          prev->flink->blink = prev->blink;
255	        }
256	
257	      /* Then merge the two chunks */
258	
259	      prevsize       += nodesize;
260	      prev->size      = prevsize | (prev->size & MM_MASK_BIT);
261	      next->preceding = prevsize;
262	      node            = prev;
263	    }
264	
265	  /* Add the merged node to the nodelist */
266	
267	  mm_addfreechunk(heap, node);
268	  kasan_bypass(bypass);
269	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_unlock(&heap->mm_lock));
270	}

42	/****************************************************************************
43	 * Name: mm_memalign
44	 *
45	 * Description:
46	 *   memalign requests more than enough space from malloc, finds a region
47	 *   within that chunk that meets the alignment request and then frees any
48	 *   leading or trailing space.
49	 *
50	 *   The alignment argument must be a power of two. 16-byte alignment is
51	 *   guaranteed by normal malloc calls.
52	 *
53	 ****************************************************************************/
54	
55	FAR void *mm_memalign(FAR struct mm_heap_s *heap, size_t alignment,
56	                      size_t size)
57	{
58	  FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *node;
59	  uintptr_t rawchunk;
60	  uintptr_t alignedchunk;
61	  size_t mask;
62	  size_t allocsize;
63	  size_t newsize;
64	  bool bypass;
65	
66	  /* Make sure that alignment is less than half max size_t */
67	
68	  if (alignment >= (SIZE_MAX / 2))
69	    {
70	      return NULL;
71	    }
72	
73	  /* Make sure that alignment is a power of 2 */
74	
75	  if ((alignment & -alignment) != alignment)
76	    {
77	      return NULL;
78	    }
79	
80	#ifdef CONFIG_MM_HEAP_MEMPOOL
81	  if (heap->mm_mpool)
82	    {
83	      node = mempool_multiple_memalign(heap->mm_mpool, alignment, size);
84	      if (node != NULL)
85	        {
86	          return node;
87	        }
88	    }
89	#endif
90	
91	  /* If this requested alinement's less than or equal to the natural
92	   * alignment of malloc, then just let malloc do the work.
93	   */
94	
95	  if (alignment <= MM_ALIGN)
96	    {
97	      FAR void *ptr = mm_malloc(heap, size);
98	      DEBUGASSERT(ptr == NULL || ((uintptr_t)ptr) % alignment == 0);
99	      return ptr;
100	    }
101	  else if (alignment < MM_MIN_CHUNK)
102	    {
103	      alignment = MM_MIN_CHUNK;
104	    }
105	
106	  mask = alignment - 1;
107	
108	  /* Adjust the size to account for (1) the size of the allocated node and
109	   * (2) to make sure that it is aligned with MM_ALIGN and its size is at
110	   * least MM_MIN_CHUNK.
111	   *
112	   * Notice that we increase the allocation size by twice the requested
113	   * alignment.  We do this so that there will be at least two valid
114	   * alignment points within the allocated memory.
115	   *
116	   * NOTE:  These are sizes given to malloc and not chunk sizes. They do
117	   * not include MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE.
118	   */
119	
120	  if (size < MM_MIN_CHUNK - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD)
121	    {
122	      size = MM_MIN_CHUNK - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD;
123	    }
124	
125	  newsize = MM_ALIGN_UP(size);         /* Make multiples of our granule size */
126	  allocsize = newsize + 2 * alignment; /* Add double full alignment size */
127	
128	  if (newsize < size || allocsize < newsize)
129	    {
130	      /* Integer overflow */
131	
132	      return NULL;
133	    }
134	
135	  /* Then malloc that size */
136	
137	  rawchunk = (uintptr_t)mm_malloc(heap, allocsize);
138	  if (rawchunk == 0)
139	    {
140	      return NULL;
141	    }
142	
143	  kasan_poison((FAR void *)rawchunk,
144	               mm_malloc_size(heap, (FAR void *)rawchunk));
145	
146	  rawchunk = (uintptr_t)kasan_clear_tag((FAR void *)rawchunk);
147	
148	  /* We need to hold the MM mutex while we muck with the chunks and
149	   * nodelist.
150	   */
151	
152	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_lock(&heap->mm_lock));
153	  bypass = kasan_bypass(true);
154	
155	  /* Get the node associated with the allocation and the next node after
156	   * the allocation.
157	   */
158	
159	  node = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)(rawchunk - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
160	  heap->mm_curused -= MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
161	
162	  /* Find the aligned subregion */
163	
164	  alignedchunk = (rawchunk + mask) & ~mask;
165	
166	  /* Check if there is free space at the beginning of the aligned chunk */
167	
168	  if (alignedchunk != rawchunk)
169	    {
170	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *newnode;
171	      FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *next;
172	      size_t precedingsize;
173	      size_t newnodesize;
174	
175	      /* Get the node the next node after the allocation. */
176	
177	      next = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
178	        ((FAR char *)node + MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node));
179	
180	      newnode = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
181	        (alignedchunk - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
182	
183	      /* Preceding size is full size of the new 'node,' including
184	       * MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE
185	       */
186	
187	      precedingsize = (uintptr_t)newnode - (uintptr_t)node;
188	
189	      /* If we were unlucky, then the alignedchunk can lie in such a position
190	       * that precedingsize < SIZEOF_NODE_FREENODE.  We can't let that happen
191	       * because we are going to cast 'node' to struct mm_freenode_s below.
192	       * This is why we allocated memory large enough to support two
193	       * alignment points.  In this case, we will simply use the second
194	       * alignment point.
195	       */
196	
197	      if (precedingsize < MM_MIN_CHUNK)
198	        {
199	          alignedchunk += alignment;
200	          newnode       = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)
201	                          (alignedchunk - MM_SIZEOF_ALLOCNODE);
202	          precedingsize = (uintptr_t)newnode - (uintptr_t)node;
203	        }
204	
205	      /* If the previous node is free, merge node and previous node, then
206	       * set up the node size.
207	       */
208	
209	      if (MM_PREVNODE_IS_FREE(node))
210	        {
211	          FAR struct mm_freenode_s *prev =
212	            (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)((FAR char *)node - node->preceding);
213	
214	          /* Remove the node.  There must be a predecessor, but there may
215	           * not be a successor node.
216	           */
217	
218	          DEBUGASSERT(prev->blink);
219	          prev->blink->flink = prev->flink;
220	          if (prev->flink)
221	            {
222	              prev->flink->blink = prev->blink;
223	            }
224	
225	          precedingsize += MM_SIZEOF_NODE(prev);
226	          node = (FAR struct mm_allocnode_s *)prev;
227	        }
228	
229	      node->size = precedingsize;
230	
231	      /* Set up the size of the new node */
232	
233	      newnodesize = (uintptr_t)next - (uintptr_t)newnode;
234	      newnode->size = newnodesize | MM_ALLOC_BIT | MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
235	      newnode->preceding = precedingsize;
236	
237	      /* Clear the previous free bit of the next node */
238	
239	      next->size &= ~MM_PREVFREE_BIT;
240	
241	      /* Convert the newnode chunk size back into malloc-compatible size by
242	       * subtracting the header size MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD.
243	       */
244	
245	      allocsize = newnodesize - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD;
246	
247	      /* Add the original, newly freed node to the free nodelist */
248	
249	      mm_addfreechunk(heap, (FAR struct mm_freenode_s *)node);
250	
251	      /* Replace the original node with the newlay realloaced,
252	       * aligned node
253	       */
254	
255	      node = newnode;
256	    }
257	
258	  /* Check if there is free space at the end of the aligned chunk. Convert
259	   * malloc-compatible chunk size to include MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD as needed
260	   * for mm_shrinkchunk.
261	   */
262	
263	  size = MM_ALIGN_UP(size + MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD);
264	
265	  if (allocsize > size)
266	    {
267	      /* Shrink the chunk by that much -- remember, mm_shrinkchunk wants
268	       * internal chunk sizes that include MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD.
269	       */
270	
271	      mm_shrinkchunk(heap, node, size);
272	    }
273	
274	  /* Update heap statistics */
275	
276	  size = MM_SIZEOF_NODE(node);
277	  heap->mm_curused += size;
278	  if (heap->mm_curused > heap->mm_maxused)
279	    {
280	      heap->mm_maxused = heap->mm_curused;
281	    }
282	
283	  sched_note_heap(NOTE_HEAP_ALLOC, heap, (FAR void *)alignedchunk, size,
284	                  heap->mm_curused);
285	
286	  kasan_bypass(bypass);
287	  DEBUGVERIFY(nxrmutex_unlock(&heap->mm_lock));
288	
289	  MM_RECORD(heap, node);
290	
291	  alignedchunk = (uintptr_t)kasan_unpoison((FAR const void *)alignedchunk,
292	                                           size - MM_ALLOCNODE_OVERHEAD);
293	  DEBUGASSERT(alignedchunk % alignment == 0);
294	  minfo("Aligned %"PRIxPTR" to %"PRIxPTR", size %zu\n",
295	        rawchunk, alignedchunk, size);
296	  return (FAR void *)alignedchunk;
297	}

根据对代码的深入分析，这个堆损坏错误有 **两个主要可疑原因**：

---

### 原因 1（最可能）：栈溢出导致堆元数据损坏

在 [sg2000_eth.c:1505](vendor/sg2000/chips/sg2000/sg2000_eth.c#L1505) 中：

```c
uint8_t tmp_buf[SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE];  // 1600 字节的栈上 VLA
```

而 defconfig 中配置的是：
- `CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACKSIZE=3072`（内核栈仅 3072 字节）
- `CONFIG_INIT_STACKSIZE=3072`（init 任务栈仅 3072 字节）

**1600 字节的 `tmp_buf` 占用了超过一半的栈空间**。当 ping 发送/接收数据包时，调用链为：

```
netdriver_transmit → netpkt_copyout → memcpy → tmp_buf[1600]
```

加上 `dcache_flush_range`、`dcache_clean_range` 等函数的栈帧，**很容易超出 3072 字节的栈限制**，导致栈向下增长时覆盖了堆的元数据区域，破坏了 heap node 的 `size` 和 `preceding` 字段。

---

### 原因 2：缓冲区大小不匹配导致堆溢出

在 [sg2000_eth.c:1505-1516](vendor/sg2000/chips/sg2000/sg2000_eth.c#L1505-L1516)：

```c
uint8_t tmp_buf[SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE];  // SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE = 1600
if (len > SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE)         // 检查上限是 1600
```

但实际 DMA TX 缓冲区大小是 `TX_BUF_SIZE = 1536`。如果数据包长度在 **1537~1600 字节**之间：
- 长度检查通过（≤ 1600）
- 数据被复制到 `tmp_buf`（1600 字节，没问题）
- 但随后 `memcpy(priv->tx_buf[idx], data, len)` 会**溢出 1536 字节的 DMA TX 缓冲区**，破坏相邻的堆节点元数据

虽然正常以太网帧最大 1514 字节不会触发，但如果有异常数据包或 VLAN 标签等情况，就可能触发。

---

### 原因 3：中断栈过小

`CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK=2048`，中断处理函数 `sg2000_interrupt` 会调用 `tx_cleanup`（包含 dcache 操作），如果同时处理 TX 和 RX 中断，栈空间可能不足。

---

### 建议修复方案

1. **消除栈上 VLA**（最关键）：将 `tmp_buf` 改为动态分配或使用静态缓冲区
2. **修复大小不匹配**：将检查改为 `TX_BUF_SIZE` 而不是 `SG2000_ETH_BUFSIZE`
3. **增大栈配置**：适当增加 `CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_STACKSIZE` 和 `CONFIG_ARCH_INTERRUPTSTACK`

## 通俗解释

### 打个比方

把**内核栈**想象成一张 **30 厘米宽的桌子**，程序运行时需要在桌子上放东西（变量）。

### 问题出在哪？

`netdriver_transmit` 函数里有一行：

```c
uint8_t tmp_buf[1600];  // 在桌子上铺了一张 1600 字节的大纸
```

这张"大纸"占了桌子的一大半。但问题是：**这张桌子不只你一个人用**——函数调用是有层级的，上层函数也把东西放在同一张桌子上。

调用链大概是这样的：

```
协议栈处理（也在用桌子）
  → eth_input（也在用桌子）
    → netdriver_transmit（铺了1600字节的大纸）
      → hw_transmit（继续用桌子）
```

桌子总共才 **3072 字节**，你一个人就占了 1600，加上其他函数的东西，**桌子放不下了，东西就掉到地上**（栈溢出）。

### "掉到地上"是什么意思？

"地上"就是**堆内存区域**——存放网络数据包、IOB 缓冲区等重要数据的地方。栈溢出后，栈上的数据**覆盖了堆里的关键信息**（比如指针、元数据）。

### 为什么 ifup 正常，ping 就崩？

- **ifup 时**：栈溢出已经发生了，但"运气好"，覆盖的堆数据暂时没被用到，所以看起来一切正常
- **ping 时**：协议栈要使用之前被破坏的指针（比如 `dev->d_private`），这个指针已经变成了垃圾值 `0x010085fa74`，CPU 去读这个地址 → **页面错误，崩溃！**

### 怎么修的？

把那张 1600 字节的"大纸"从桌子上拿掉。数据本来就要复制到 DMA 缓冲区的，直接复制过去就行，不需要先放在栈上再搬一次。

```
修改前：数据 → tmp_buf（栈上1600字节）→ DMA缓冲区  （两次搬运，栈溢出）
修改后：数据 → DMA缓冲区                           （一次搬运，安全）
```

1. **ARP 包确实发出去了**：42 字节（正确的 ARP 包大小），发了 4 次（desc[0]~desc[3]，重试了 4 次）

### 关键线索

```
dma_status=0x00170004  → 第一次TX：TU=1（TX buffer unavailable），还没发完
dma_status=0x00170405  → 后续TX：TI=1（TX完成），RI=1（收到了数据）
```

**RI=1 说明 DMA 确实收到了数据包**，但日志里没有任何 RX 处理的打印。这意味着：

**1. RX 中断处理链断裂**

DMA 收到包 → 触发中断 → ISR 调用 `netdev_lower_rxready()` → 入队 work → `netdriver_receive()` 被调用 → 交给协议栈

这条链上某一环断了。最可能的是 `netdriver_receive()` 没有被调用，或者返回了 NULL。

**2. RX 描述符 OWN 位没有正确清除**

如果 `netdriver_receive()` 读取描述符时发现 OWN 位仍然属于 DMA，就会返回 NULL，认为没有包。

**3. 缓存一致性问题**

RX 描述符或 RX 缓冲区的 dcache invalidate 没有正确执行，CPU 读到的是旧的缓存数据，看不到 DMA 写入的新包。

在 `netdriver_receive()` 入口加一行打印，看看它有没有被调用，以及描述符的状态：

```c

```

- `netdriver_receive()` 是否被调用了
- 描述符的 OWN 位是什么状态
- 是"没被调用"还是"调用了但认为没包"

找到问题了！看这一行：

```c
priv->tx_buf_phys[i] = (uintptr_t)priv->tx_buf[i];  // line 791
```

**这里把虚拟地址当成了物理地址！**

你的 defconfig 中配置了：
```
CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_HEAP_BASE=0xC0000000
CONFIG_ARCH_KERNEL_HEAP_SIZE=0x200000
```

内核堆的虚拟地址是 `0xC0000000`，但物理地址应该是 `0x80200000`。`kmm_memalign` 返回的是虚拟地址（`0xC0XXXXXX`），但 DMA 引擎需要的是物理地址（`0x80XXXXXX`）。

## 验证

从日志看 `des2=0x8042BDC0`，这确实是物理地址范围。但代码直接赋值 `priv->tx_buf_phys[i] = (uintptr_t)priv->tx_buf[i]`，如果堆在 `0xC0000000`，那 `priv->tx_buf[i]` 应该是 `0xC0XXXXXX`，不应该出现 `0x80XXXXXX`。

这说明你的系统可能确实是 identity mapping（虚拟=物理），或者堆在 `0x80200000`。

**你能确认一下 `priv->tx_buf[0]` 的实际值吗？** 在 `hw_transmit` 中加一行：

```c
ethinfo("TX buf[%u] virt=%p phys=0x%08" PRIX32 "\n", idx, priv->tx_buf[idx], priv->tx_buf_phys[idx]);
```

这样就能确认虚拟地址和物理地址是否一致。如果虚拟地址是 `0xC0XXXXXX` 而物理地址也赋成了 `0xC0XXXXXX`，那 DMA 就会读到错误的数据。

RISC-V 的中断映射关系：

  int extirq;

  if (irq == RISCV_IRQ_SOFT)
    {
      /* Read sstatus & set software interrupt enable in sie */

      SET_CSR(CSR_IE, IE_SIE);
    }
  else if (irq == RISCV_IRQ_TIMER)
    {
      /* Read sstatus & set timer interrupt enable in sie */

      SET_CSR(CSR_IE, IE_TIE);
    }
  else if (irq > RISCV_IRQ_EXT)
    {
      extirq = irq - RISCV_IRQ_EXT;

      /* Set enable bit for the irq */

      if (0 <= extirq && extirq <= 63)
        {
          modifyreg32(SG2000_PLIC_ENABLE1 + (4 * (extirq / 32)),
                      0, 1 << (extirq % 32));
        }
      else
        {
          PANIC();
        }
    }
}

## 通俗解释

### 打个比方

把中断系统想象成一个**酒店的房间号**：

```
酒店楼层布局：
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  1楼: 特殊房间（系统保留）                  │
│     房间 0-15: 系统异常（硬件故障等）        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  2楼: 软件中断                              │
│     房间 16: 软件中断                       │
│     房间 17-24: 保留                       │
├─────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  3楼: 外部设备中断（PLIC 管理）              │
│     房间 25 = 外部中断 0                    │
│     房间 26 = 外部中断 1                    │
│     ...                                   │
│     房间 56 = 外部中断 31  ← ETH 网卡！     │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### 为什么是 +31？

**PLIC（中断控制器）给每个设备编号**：
- UART 串口 = 设备 69
- **ETH 网卡 = 设备 31**（手册里写的）

**但 NuttX 的"房间号"不是从0开始的**：
- 前 25 个"房间"被系统占用了（异常、软件中断等）
- 外部设备从第 25 号"房间"开始分配

所以：

```
NuttX 房间号 = RISCV_IRQ_EXT + PLIC设备号
             = 25 + 31
             = 56
```

### 之前的错误

之前用 `NVIC_IRQ_FIRST + 15 = 31`，这相当于：
```
PLIC设备号 = 31 - 25 = 6
```
让系统去使能**设备 6** 的中断，但 ETH 实际是**设备 31**，所以中断永远触发不了！

### 简单公式

```
NuttX逻辑IRQ号 = 25 + 手册上的PLIC中断号
```

手册说 ETH 是 PLIC 中断 31 → NuttX 就用 `25 + 31 = 56`。
